elements.content: Grammar focus: Literary & Formal Sentence Patterns.

Core Rule: Build periodic sentences by withholding the main independent clause until the final position: [Subordinate Clauses / Prepositional Phrases] + Main Independent Clause .

Periodic Sentence — Holds main idea until sentence conclusion: Despite mounting opposition, declining revenues, and public skepticism, the CEO reaffirmed the strategy .
Balanced Antithesis — Symmetrical clauses expressing opposing ideas: Not that I loved Caesar less , but that I loved Rome more .
Parallelism (Isocolon) — Identical grammatical structure in successive phrases: To think clearly , to write concisely , and to speak persuasively are C2 goals.
Chiasmus — Inverted repetition of syntactic elements (A-B-B-A): Ask not what your country can do for you ; ask what you can do for your country .
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence follows a classic periodic structure?
options: After years of rigorous research and relentless experimentation, the breakthrough occurred.
The breakthrough occurred after years of research and experimentation.

elements.content: 2. What defines grammatical parallelism?
options: Using identical grammatical forms for coordinated elements
Mixing gerunds and infinitives in the same list
